items.content:
US homebuyers are walking away from deals at the highest rate in years:

14.0% of home-purchase agreements that went under contract fell through in July, the highest rate since November 2023.

The national cancellation rate has held between 13.0% and 14.0% over the last 4 years, well above the lower rates typical of the seller's market from 2020 to 2022.

Atlanta posted the highest cancellation rate last month, at 19.8%, followed by Houston at 19.6%, San Antonio at 18.7%, and Las Vegas at 18.6%.

This comes as sellers outnumber buyers by ~51%, near the highest percentage on record, giving buyers more options and making them more willing to walk away over inspection issues, low appraisals, or rejected concessions.

At the same time, high home prices and elevated mortgage rates are leaving buyers with less financial room, making unexpected costs or concerns about taking on large monthly payments more likely to derail deals.

The housing market is under historic pressure.
— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) Sep 8, 2026

items.title: Non-asset owners are very worried about inflation. The 3-month moving average of 1-year inflation expectations among US consumers with no stock holdings hit ~5.0% in August, near the highest level this year. This is significantly above the ~3.0% recorded in late 2024. Meanwhile, the 3-month moving average of inflation expectations among US consumers with the largest stock holdings remained below 4.0% last month. Readings for both groups were roughly in-line with levels seen in late-2022, following the recovery from the energy crisis. Asset owners are the only winners in this economy.

items.title: Russian gold flows into Hong Kong are skyrocketing: In the first 7 months of 2026, Hong Kong’s gold imports from Russia rose to $14.4 billion. This is already +50% above the full-year figure of $9.6 billion recorded in 2025. This is also nearly triple the amount seen in 2023 and 2024. The surge reflects the redirection of Russian gold exports toward Asian markets after Western sanctions effectively closed London and other Western hubs to Russian bullion. Hong Kong has no such restrictions, allowing it to increasingly serve as a major trading hub for Russian gold entering the Asian market. The flow of Russian gold into Asia is accelerating.

items.content:
The de-dollarization trend appears to be far from global:

The US Dollar’s proportion of official global FX reserves is down to 57%, its lowest in at least 30 years.

This percentage has declined -20 points since 1999, with China and, to a lesser extent, Russia driving much of the decline.

Over the same period, the combined proportion of the 4 major reserve currencies, the US Dollar, Yen, Euro and Pound, has fallen -12 percentage points, to ~87%, also its lowest in at least 30 years.

Meanwhile, roughly equal numbers of countries increased and decreased their US Dollar reserves between 2015 and 2023.

Therefore, the decline is heavily concentrated among a small number of reserve holders, suggesting the US Dollar's position in most reserve portfolios remains relatively stable.

The threat to the US Dollar’s reserve currency status appears limited.
— The Kobeissi Letter (@KobeissiLetter) Sep 7, 2026

items.title: What is happening with the US job market? US job openings for June were revised down by -177,000 vacancies, their largest monthly downward revision since November 2025. This also marks the 3rd consecutive monthly downward revision. Furthermore, the number of hires for June was revised down by -16,000, while the number of quits was revised lower by -19,000. At the same time, the number of layoffs and discharges was revised up by +19,000. As a result, job openings have now been revised down in 38 of the last 43 months. US labor market data is becoming increasingly difficult to read with confidence.
